title: Cornbread with honey butter

stages.title: Prepare the batter
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C and grease a 20 cm square baking tin.
Whisk cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in one bowl; beat eggs, buttermilk, melted butter and 1 tbsp honey in another.

stages.title: Combine gently
steps: Pour wet ingredients into dry and fold just until no dry flour remains.
Do not overmix; a few small lumps are fine.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Spread batter in the tin and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cutting.

stages.title: Make honey butter
steps: Beat softened butter with remaining honey and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Serve a little over each warm square.

quick_steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C and grease a 20 cm square tin. Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in one bowl.
Beat the eggs, buttermilk, melted butter and 1 tbsp honey in another bowl.
Fold the wet mix into the dry until no dry flour remains. A few small lumps are fine.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Beat the softened butter with the remaining honey and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Cut the cornbread into squares and serve warm with a little honey butter on each.

title: Turkey and avocado wraps

stages.title: Mix the spread
steps: Mash avocado with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Stir mustard into yoghurt in a separate bowl for a tangy dressing.

stages.title: Prepare fillings
steps: Wash and dry lettuce thoroughly, slice tomatoes and grate carrot.
Lay turkey slices out so they are ready to assemble quickly.

stages.title: Assemble wraps
steps: Spread avocado over the centre of each tortilla, leaving a border.
Layer lettuce, turkey, tomato and carrot, then drizzle with yoghurt dressing.

stages.title: Roll and serve
steps: Fold the sides inward and roll tightly from the bottom, keeping fillings tucked in.
Cut diagonally with a sharp knife and serve immediately.

quick_steps: Mash the avocados with lemon juice and a pinch of salt. In a separate bowl, stir the Dijon mustard into the Greek yoghurt for the dressing.
Wash and dry the lettuce, slice the tomatoes and grate the carrot.
Spread the avocado over the centre of each tortilla, leaving a border. Layer on the lettuce, turkey, tomato and carrot, then drizzle with the dressing.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly from the bottom. Cut diagonally with a sharp knife and serve straight away.

title: Ginataang kalabasa

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Cook onion in oil over medium heat until translucent, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in fish sauce and 100 ml water.

stages.title: Cook pumpkin
steps: Add pumpkin and simmer covered for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Pour in coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Finish beans
steps: Add green beans and cook 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season to taste and serve with rice.

quick_steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until translucent, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the fish sauce and 100 ml water.
Add the pumpkin, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the green beans and cook for 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season to taste and serve with rice, if using.

title: Minestrone

stages.title: Sweat vegetables
steps: Heat oil and cook onion, carrot and celery over medium-low heat until softened.
Add garlic and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

stages.title: Build soup
steps: Add tomatoes, stock and courgette, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook until vegetables are nearly tender.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Stir in drained beans and pasta.
Simmer until pasta is al dente, adding water if the soup thickens too much.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

quick_steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for about 10 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock and courgette and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for about 20 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Stir in the cannellini beans and pasta. Simmer for about 10 minutes until the pasta is al dente, adding water if the soup gets too thick.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Chicken cacciatore

stages.title: Brown chicken
steps: Season thighs with salt and pepper and brown in olive oil over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes until golden.
Turn once to colour both sides, then set aside on a plate.

stages.title: Cook vegetables
steps: Add sliced onion, capsicum and mushrooms to the same pan.
Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, then add minced garlic and oregano.

stages.title: Deglaze and simmer
steps: Pour in wine, scraping the base, and simmer for 3 minutes before adding tomatoes and stock.
Return chicken, cover loosely and simmer gently until chicken reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Reduce and finish
steps: Uncover and simmer until sauce coats a spoon rather than pooling thinly.
Taste for salt and acidity, then serve with polenta or crusty bread.

quick_steps: Season the chicken thighs with salt and brown in olive oil over medium-high heat, turning once, about 5 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Cook the sliced onion, capsicum and mushrooms in the same pan until the mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown. Add the garlic and oregano.
Pour in the wine, scraping the base, and simmer for 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and stock.
Return the chicken, cover loosely and simmer gently until it reaches 75°C.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon. Season with salt to taste and serve with polenta or crusty bread.

title: Chicken fajitas

stages.title: Slice and season
steps: Cut chicken into even thin strips and slice peppers and onion to a similar thickness.
Toss chicken with half the oil, spices, salt and lime zest; keep raw chicken separate from vegetables.

stages.title: Cook the vegetables
steps: Heat a large frying pan until hot, add remaining oil and cook peppers and onion in batches.
Let them char lightly before stirring so they develop colour while retaining some bite.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Transfer vegetables to a plate and add chicken in a single layer.
Cook, turning, until golden and the thickest pieces reach 74°C; return vegetables and squeeze over lime juice.

stages.title: Serve hot
steps: Warm tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Serve the sizzling filling with sour cream and sliced avocado.

quick_steps: Slice the chicken, peppers and red onion into thin strips. Toss the chicken with half the olive oil, paprika, cumin, oregano, salt and lime zest.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Cook the peppers and onion in batches until lightly charred but still with some bite.
Move the vegetables to a plate. Cook the chicken in a single layer over high heat, turning, until golden and 74°C in the thickest pieces.
Return the vegetables to the pan and squeeze over the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or in foil in the oven. Serve the filling with sour cream and sliced avocado.

title: Brik
ingredients: 2 potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add the salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and leave in the colander to steam dry for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Mash the potatoes coarsely in a bowl, leaving some small lumps.
Stir in the tuna, parsley, capers, lemon zest and black pepper.
Divide the filling into 4 portions.

stages.title: Fill and fold the pastry
steps: Lay 1 sheet of filo flat, keeping the others covered with a damp tea towel. Fold it in half to make a double-layer rectangle, or stack 2 sheets if yours are thin.
Spoon 1 portion of filling onto one half of the pastry, shaping it into a ring with a well in the centre.
Crack 1 egg into the well, being careful not to break the yolk.
Fold the pastry over to form a half-moon and press the edges firmly to seal, brushing with a little water if needed. Repeat with the remaining pastry, filling and eggs.

stages.title: Fry and serve
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a pinch of pastry sizzles on contact.

Carefully slide in 1 brik and fry for 1–2 minutes on each side, spooning hot oil over the top, until the pastry is golden and crisp and the egg white is set and the yolk is runny, or cooked through if you prefer for a little longer.
Lift out onto paper towel to drain and repeat with the remaining briks, one at a time, reheating the oil briefly between batches.
Serve straight away with the lemon wedges.

quick_steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 5 minutes.
Coarsely mash the potatoes, leaving small lumps, then mix in the tuna, parsley, capers, lemon zest and pepper. Divide into 4 portions.
Fold a filo sheet in half (or stack 2 if thin). Shape a portion of filling into a ring with a well, then crack an egg into the well.
Fold the pastry into a half-moon and press the edges to seal. Repeat with the remaining filo, filling and eggs.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a pinch of pastry sizzles. Fry the briks one at a time, 1–2 minutes a side, until golden and the egg white is set.
Drain on paper towel and serve straight away with the lemon wedges.

title: Congee with ginger chicken

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Rinse rice until water runs mostly clear.
Slice ginger and spring onions; cut chicken into two even pieces.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Combine rice, stock and ginger in a saucepan; simmer uncovered on low heat 45–55 minutes, stirring often, until grains break down.
Add chicken for the final 15–20 minutes, still on low heat, and cook through.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove chicken and shred with forks.
Return to porridge, adjust thickness with hot water and season with soy and salt; finish with spring onion and sesame oil.

quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Slice the ginger and spring onions, and cut the chicken into two even pieces.
Combine the rice, stock and ginger in a saucepan. Simmer uncovered on low heat for 45–55 minutes, until the grains break down.
Add the chicken for the final 15–20 minutes, until cooked through.
Remove the chicken and shred it with forks.
Return the chicken to the congee and thin with hot water. Season with the soy sauce and salt.
Finish with the spring onion and sesame oil.

title: Spanish tortilla

stages.title: Slice potatoes and onion
steps: Peel potatoes and slice into thin even rounds; thinly slice onion.
Beat eggs in a large bowl with salt and pepper until combined, without incorporating too much air.

stages.title: Gently cook potatoes
steps: Heat olive oil in a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add potatoes and onion and cook gently, stirring occasionally, until completely tender but not browned; drain off most oil.

stages.title: Combine and set
steps: Fold warm potato mixture into eggs and rest 3 minutes.
Return to a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low heat and cook until edges set and centre is mostly firm.

stages.title: Flip and finish
steps: Place a flat plate over the pan and carefully invert the tortilla, using oven gloves.
Slide back into the pan and cook until set through; rest 5 minutes before slicing.

quick_steps: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and onion. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a large bowl until just combined.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Cook the potatoes and onion gently until completely tender but not browned, then drain off most of the oil.
Fold the warm potato mixture into the eggs and rest for 3 minutes.
Cook in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low heat until the edges set and the centre is mostly firm.
Invert onto a plate, slide back into the pan and cook until set through. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Galaktoboureko

stages.title: Prepare the pan, butter and lemon
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Melt the butter and use a little to grease a 20 x 25 cm baking dish.
Remove the zest from the lemon in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, then juice the lemon.
Cover the filo sheets with a damp tea towel so they don't dry out.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Combine the milk, semolina and 75 g of the sugar in a medium saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture is thick and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla extract and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs until smooth.

stages.title: Assemble the pie
steps: Lay 5 filo sheets in the dish one at a time, brushing each with melted butter and letting the edges overhang.
Pour in the custard and spread it evenly.
Fold the overhanging filo over the custard, then layer the remaining 5 sheets on top, brushing each with melted butter.
Tuck in the edges, brush the top with the remaining butter and score the top layers into squares with a sharp knife, cutting only through the filo.

stages.title: Bake and make the syrup
steps: Bake for 35–40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the custard is set with only a slight wobble in the centre.
While it bakes, combine the water, the remaining 75 g sugar, the lemon zest strips and 1 tbsp of the lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy, then remove the zest and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Soak and rest
steps: Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the pastry as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Rest for at least 30 minutes so the syrup soaks in and the custard firms up.
Cut along the scored lines and serve warm or at room temperature.

quick_steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 20 x 25 cm dish with a little of the melted butter, strip the zest from the lemon and juice it, and keep the filo under a damp tea towel.
Whisk the milk, semolina and half the sugar in a saucepan over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the vanilla, cool 5 minutes, then whisk in the eggs.
Layer 5 buttered filo sheets in the dish, letting the edges overhang. Pour in the custard, fold the edges over, then top with 5 more buttered sheets.
Tuck in the edges, brush with the remaining butter and score into squares. Bake 35–40 minutes until deep golden and just set with a slight wobble.
Meanwhile, simmer the water, remaining sugar, zest strips and 1 tbsp lemon juice over medium heat for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy. Remove the zest and cool.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot pastry and rest at least 30 minutes. Cut along the scored lines and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Frittata di zucchine

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and eggs
steps: Slice the zucchini into thin rounds about 3 mm thick and thinly slice the onion.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk with a fork until the yolks and whites are combined.
Stir in the parmesan, the salt, the pepper and half the torn basil leaves.

stages.title: Cook the onion and zucchini
steps: Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick ovenproof frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook, stirring often, for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated from the pan.

stages.title: Set the frittata
steps: Heat the grill to high with the rack positioned about 15 cm from the element.
Spread the vegetables evenly over the base of the pan and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes, without stirring, until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Place the pan under the grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set and no longer wobbles.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the frittata in the pan for 3 minutes so it firms up for slicing.
Scatter the remaining basil over the top and cut into 4 wedges.

quick_steps: Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, salt, pepper and half the torn basil. Thinly slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds and the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a 24 cm ovenproof non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the vegetables over the pan, reduce to medium-low, pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre no longer wobbles.
Rest in the pan for 3 minutes, scatter over the remaining basil and cut into 4 wedges.

title: Oi muchim (cucumber salad)

stages.title: Slice cucumbers
steps: Cut cucumbers into thin rounds or half-moons.
Toss with salt in a colander and leave for 10 minutes to draw out moisture.

stages.title: Drain and dry
steps: Rinse lightly if very salty, then pat cucumbers dry with kitchen paper.
Drying prevents the dressing becoming diluted.

stages.title: Mix spicy dressing
steps: Stir gochugaru, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil until combined.
Slice spring onion finely and add it to the dressing.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Coat cucumbers evenly and sprinkle sesame seeds on top.
Serve promptly while crisp, or chill briefly before eating.

quick_steps: Cut the cucumbers into thin rounds or half-moons, toss with the salt in a colander and leave for 10 minutes.
Rinse lightly if very salty, then pat the cucumbers dry with kitchen paper.
Mix the gochugaru, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil, then add the finely sliced spring onion.
Toss the cucumbers in the dressing until evenly coated, then sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Serve while crisp, or chill briefly.

title: Shirazi salad
ingredients: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, cut into 1 cm dice
4 tomatoes, cored and cut into 1 cm dice

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the cucumbers into 1 cm dice and place them in a large bowl.
Cut the tomatoes in half, scoop out the watery seeds and cores with a teaspoon, then dice the flesh into 1 cm pieces and add to the bowl.
Finely chop the red onion and add it to the bowl.

stages.title: Mellow the onion
steps: Sprinkle the onion and vegetables with the salt and toss gently.
Leave the bowl to stand at room temperature for 10 minutes so the onion softens and loses its harshness.
Tip off any liquid that has pooled at the bottom of the bowl.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Whisk the lime juice, olive oil and dried mint in a small bowl, rubbing the mint between your fingers as you add it to release its flavour.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve straight away while the vegetables are still crisp.

quick_steps: Dice the cucumbers and tomatoes into 1 cm pieces, scooping the watery seeds from the tomatoes, and finely chop the red onion. Combine in a large bowl.
Toss the vegetables with the salt and leave for 1 minute, until the onion softens. Tip off any pooled liquid.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil and dried mint, rubbing the mint between your fingers as you add it.
Pour the dressing over, toss to coat and season with black pepper and extra salt if needed. Serve straight away while crisp.

title: Caprese stuffed peppers
ingredients: 4 capsicums, halved lengthways through the stem, seeds removed
250 g mozzarella, drained and torn into small pieces
1 bunch basil, leaves picked, larger leaves torn

stages.title: Prepare the capsicums and oven
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Halve the capsicums lengthways through the stems and scrape out the seeds and white membranes, keeping the stems on so the halves hold their shape.
Place the capsicums cut side up on the tray, brush the insides and edges with half the olive oil and season with half the salt.

stages.title: Roast the capsicums
steps: Roast the capsicums on the middle shelf for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to colour and the flesh has softened slightly.
Remove the tray from the oven and leave the oven on at 200°C (180°C fan) for the second bake.

stages.title: Make the tomato filling
steps: While the capsicums roast, combine the cherry tomatoes, garlic, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, the remaining salt and a good grind of black pepper in a bowl.
Stir through half the basil leaves.
Tip any liquid out of the roasted capsicum halves if it has pooled, then spoon the tomato mixture into them.

stages.title: Bake with the mozzarella
steps: Scatter the torn mozzarella over the tomato filling.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese has melted and is lightly golden in spots and the capsicums are tender when pierced with a knife.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until syrupy and able to coat the back of a spoon.
Let the capsicums stand for 3 minutes, then drizzle with the balsamic syrup and top with the remaining basil.

quick_steps: Heat the oven to 240°C (180°C fan). Put the seeded capsicum halves cut side up on a lined tray, brush with half the olive oil and season with half the salt.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the edges start to colour and the flesh softens slightly.
Meanwhile, mix the cherry tomatoes, garlic, remaining oil and salt, pepper and half the basil. Tip any pooled liquid from the capsicums, then spoon in the filling.
Top with the torn mozzarella and bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and lightly golden and the capsicums are tender.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until syrupy.
Rest the capsicums for 3 minutes, then drizzle with the balsamic syrup and top with the remaining basil.

title: Cajun shrimp and grits

stages.title: Cook grits
steps: Bring stock and milk to a simmer and whisk in grits gradually.
Cook according to packet, stirring frequently until creamy; stir in cheddar.

stages.title: Prepare prawns
steps: Pat prawns dry and toss with Cajun seasoning.
Chop capsicum, garlic and spring onions while grits cook.

stages.title: Sauté topping
steps: Heat butter and oil in a pan over medium-high heat and soften capsicum for 3 minutes.
Add garlic and prawns; cook for 2 to 3 minutes until prawns turn pink, opaque and firm.

stages.title: Serve immediately
steps: Loosen grits with warm water if needed and spoon into bowls.
Top with prawns, pan juices and sliced spring onions.

quick_steps: Pat the prawns dry and toss with the Cajun seasoning. Chop the capsicum, garlic and spring onions.
Heat the butter and oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the capsicum for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink, opaque and firm.
Loosen the grits with a little warm water if needed and spoon into bowls. Top with the prawns, pan juices and sliced spring onions.
note: dropped: 'Simmer the stock and milk over medium heat, whisk in the gri'

title: Chimichurri steak
ingredients: 700 g beef steak, such as rump, about 3 cm thick
1 bunch parsley, leaves picked and finely chopped

stages.title: Make the chimichurri
steps: Combine the chopped parsley and garlic in a bowl with the red wine vinegar, 60 ml of the olive oil, the dried oregano, the chilli flakes and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Stir well, then leave at room temperature for 20 minutes so the garlic mellows and the flavours blend.

stages.title: Season the steak
steps: Pat the steak dry with paper towel so it browns rather than steams.
Rub the steak all over with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the black pepper.
Leave the steak at room temperature for 15 minutes while the chimichurri sits.

stages.title: Cook the steak
steps: Heat a heavy frying pan or chargrill pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes on one side without moving it, until deeply browned.
Turn and cook for another 3–4 minutes for medium-rare, until browned outside and still pink in the middle. Cook longer if you prefer it more done.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Move the steak to a board and rest it, loosely covered with foil, for 10 minutes.
Slice the steak across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Spoon the chimichurri over the sliced steak and serve with the resting juices.

quick_steps: Mix the parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, 60 ml olive oil, oregano, chilli flakes and half the salt. Leave for 20 minutes so the flavours blend.
Pat the steak dry and rub with the remaining salt and the pepper. Rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining olive oil.
Spoon the chimichurri over the steak and serve with the resting juices.
Rest the steak under foil for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes without moving it, until deeply browned. Turn and cook 3–4 minutes more for medium-rare, still pink in the middle.
note: order: step 4 and the last step swapped

title: Misir wot

stages.title: Cook onions slowly
steps: Cook onions in a dry heavy pot over medium-low heat, stirring often until softened and golden.
Add oil once they begin to catch, then continue until sweet and reduced.

stages.title: Bloom spices
steps: Stir in garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste.
Cook briefly over low heat until fragrant, adding a splash of water to prevent scorching.

stages.title: Simmer lentils
steps: Add rinsed lentils and water, stirring well to release the spiced onion base.
Simmer gently, stirring frequently, until lentils break down into a thick stew.

stages.title: Adjust texture
steps: Add hot water a little at a time if the stew becomes too stiff.
Season and serve with injera or rice.

quick_steps: Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until softened and golden. Add the olive oil once they catch and cook until sweet and reduced.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste. Cook over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant, adding a splash of water if it scorches.
Add the lentils and water. Bake gently for about 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils break down into a thick stew.
Loosen with a little hot water if the stew gets too stiff. Season with the salt.
Serve with rice or injera.

title: Quiche Lorraine

stages.title: Blind-bake pastry
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional and press pastry into a 23 cm tart tin.
Line with baking paper and weights, bake 15 minutes, then remove weights and bake 5 minutes more.

stages.title: Cook bacon
steps: Fry bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and fat renders.
Drain on kitchen paper so the filling does not become greasy.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper until just combined, avoiding excessive foam.
Scatter bacon and cheese evenly over the baked pastry case.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Pour custard into the tart and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until edges are set and centre gently wobbles.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing so the custard firms without drying.

quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Press the pastry into a 23 cm tart tin, line with baking paper and weights, and bake 15 minutes. Remove the weights and bake 5 minutes more.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and the fat has rendered. Drain on kitchen paper.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper until just combined, without making it foamy.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the baked pastry case, then pour in the custard.
Bake at 180°C for 1 minute, until the edges are set and the centre just wobbles.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Sicilian caponata

stages.title: Brown aubergine
steps: Dice aubergine into 2 cm cubes and toss with half the olive oil.
Roast at 220°C until golden and soft, turning once.

stages.title: Soften vegetables
steps: Heat remaining oil in a wide pan and cook diced onion and celery over medium heat for about 8 minutes.
Stir occasionally until tender but not browned.

stages.title: Build sweet-sour sauce
steps: Add tomatoes, olives, rinsed capers, vinegar and sugar.
Simmer gently until tomatoes thicken and flavours balance, adjusting vinegar or sugar a little at a time.

stages.title: Combine and rest
steps: Fold roasted aubergine through the sauce without crushing the pieces.
Rest at least 10 minutes and finish with parsley; serve warm or at room temperature.

quick_steps: Dice the aubergines into 2 cm cubes, toss with half the olive oil and roast at 120°C until golden and soft, turning once.
Cook the diced onion and celery in the remaining oil in a wide pan over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until tender but not browned.
Add the tomatoes, olives, rinsed capers, vinegar and sugar, then simmer gently until the tomatoes thicken. Adjust the vinegar or sugar to taste.
Gently fold the roasted aubergine through the sauce, then rest for at least 10 minutes.
Finish with the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Kheer rice pudding

stages.title: Soak the rice and prepare the flavourings
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cover the rice with cold water in a bowl and soak for 15 minutes, then drain well.
While the rice soaks, lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife so they split open.
Roughly chop the pistachios and set aside.

stages.title: Simmer the milk with the rice
steps: Pour the milk into a large heavy-based saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until small bubbles form around the edge, about 8 minutes.
Add the drained rice, crushed cardamom pods and saffron threads, and stir well.
Bring back to a gentle simmer, about 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low.

stages.title: Cook until thick and creamy
steps: Cook over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring every 3–4 minutes and scraping the base of the pan so the milk does not catch.
When the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced to a thick, creamy consistency, stir in the sugar.
Cook for a further 5 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar has dissolved and the kheer coats the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and fish out the cardamom pods.
Stir in the rosewater and let the kheer rest for 10 minutes; it will thicken further as it cools.
Spoon into 4 bowls and scatter with the chopped pistachios. Serve warm.

quick_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then soak in cold water for 15 minutes and drain. Lightly crush the cardamom pods so they split open.
Heat the milk in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat until small bubbles form around the edge, about 8 minutes.
Cook on low for 35 minutes, stirring often and scraping the base, until the rice is very soft and the milk is thick and creamy.
Stir in the sugar and cook 5 more minutes, until dissolved and the kheer coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the cardamom pods and stir in the rosewater. Rest for 10 minutes, then serve warm topped with the chopped pistachios.
note: dropped: 'Add the rice, cardamom and saffron. Bring to a gentle simmer'

title: Congee with ginger

stages.title: Rinse rice
steps: Rinse rice briefly and drain.
Place in a heavy saucepan with stock and sliced ginger.

stages.title: Simmer gently
steps: Bring to a boil, then lower to a very gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for about 50 minutes, until the rice begins to break down, stirring occasionally so rice does not stick to the base.

stages.title: Adjust texture
steps: Continue cooking until grains break down and porridge is thick and silky.
Add hot water to loosen if needed, then season with soy sauce and white pepper.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Remove large ginger slices and ladle congee into bowls.
Top with sliced eggs, spring onions and a few drops of sesame oil.

quick_steps: Rinse the jasmine rice and drain. Put it in a heavy saucepan with the stock and sliced ginger.
Top with sliced eggs, spring onions and a few drops of sesame oil.
Cook uncovered for about 50 minutes, until the rice starts to break down, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick.
Keep cooking for about 10 minutes, until the congee is thick and silky. Loosen with hot water if needed, then season with the soy sauce and white pepper.
Remove the large ginger slices and ladle the congee into bowls.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to low for a very gentle simmer.

title: Vietnamese caramelised pork bowls

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and cucumber
steps: Finely chop the garlic and shallots and keep them together in a small bowl.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds and cut the lime into wedges.
Measure the brown sugar into a small saucepan and measure the fish sauce into a small jug, ready to use.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the rice according to the packet, over low heat once boiling, until tender, then keep it covered off the heat until the pork is ready.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Add 1 tbsp water to the brown sugar in the saucepan and heat over medium heat, without stirring, for 3–4 minutes until deep amber.
Stand back and carefully add 3 tbsp warm water, as the caramel will splutter. Stir over low heat for 1 minute until smooth, then stir in the fish sauce and remove from the heat.

stages.title: Cook the pork
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the pork mince and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and no longer pink.
Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the caramel and add the black pepper. Simmer over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the pork.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls and spoon the pork and its sauce over the top.
Add the cucumber slices and a lime wedge to each bowl, and squeeze the lime over just before eating.

quick_steps: Finely chop the garlic and shallots, slice the cucumber and cut the lime into wedges.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook per the packet over low heat once boiling, until tender. Keep covered off the heat.

Heat the brown sugar with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over medium heat, without stirring, for 3–4 minutes until deep amber. Carefully add 3 tbsp warm water, stir over low heat until smooth, then add the fish sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 5–6 minutes until browned and no longer pink. Add the shallots and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the caramel and black pepper and bake over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until thick and glossy. Serve over the rice with the cucumber and lime.

title: Cassoulet-inspired white beans

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Heat oven to 190°C.
Drain beans, dice vegetables and slice sausages into large pieces.

stages.title: Build the flavours
steps: Brown sausages in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes and set aside.
Soften onion and carrots in remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes; add garlic, tomatoes, thyme, beans and stock.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Return sausages to the pan, simmer 10 minutes, then transfer to a baking dish.
Scatter breadcrumbs and bake uncovered 25 minutes until bubbling and golden.

quick_steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Drain the beans, dice the onion and carrots, and slice the sausages into large pieces.
Brown the sausages in 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 6 minutes until browned all over. Set aside.
Soften the onion and carrots in the remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, thyme, beans and stock.
Return the sausages to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the sausages are cooked through, then transfer to a baking dish.
Scatter over the breadcrumbs and bake uncovered for 1 minute, until bubbling and golden.

title: Portokalopita

stages.title: Dry the filo
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Tear the filo pastry sheets into rough 3–4 cm pieces and spread them over the tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until dry and crisp but not coloured.
Cool the filo on the tray for 20 minutes, then crush any large pieces slightly with your hands.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Grease a 20 cm square or round cake tin with the 1 tsp olive oil and line the base with baking paper.
Finely grate the zest of 2 oranges, then juice those 2 oranges and set the juice aside for the syrup.
Whisk the eggs and 100 g of the sugar in a large bowl for 2 minutes until pale and slightly thick.
Whisk in the Greek yoghurt, the 150 ml olive oil, the orange zest, the vanilla extract and the baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the cooled filo until every piece is coated, then pour the mixture into the tin and level the top.

stages.title: Bake the cake and make the syrup
steps: Bake the cake in the oven at 180°C (160°C fan) for 40–45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
While the cake bakes, juice the remaining orange and combine it with the reserved orange juice, the remaining 150 g sugar and the 200 ml water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 8–10 minutes until lightly syrupy.
Take the syrup off the heat and leave it to cool to warm while the cake finishes.

stages.title: Soak and serve
steps: Leave the cake in its tin on a wire rack for 10 minutes, until warm rather than hot.
Pour the warm syrup slowly over the cake, a little at a time so it soaks in evenly.
Let the cake absorb the syrup for 30 minutes, then cut into 4 portions.

quick_steps: Heat the oven to 240°C (160°C fan). Tear the filo into 3–4 cm pieces and bake on a lined tray for 10–12 minutes until dry and crisp but not coloured, then cool for 20 minutes.
Grease and line a 20 cm tin with 1 tsp olive oil. Zest and juice 2 oranges, keeping the juice for the syrup.
Whisk the eggs and 100 g sugar for 2 minutes until pale and thick. Whisk in the yoghurt, 150 ml olive oil, zest, vanilla and baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the cooled filo until coated, then pour into the tin and level. Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 40–45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile, juice the last orange and simmer it with the reserved juice, remaining 150 g sugar and 200 ml water in a saucepan over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until lightly syrupy. Cool to warm.
Rest the cake in its tin for 10 minutes until warm, then slowly pour over the warm syrup. Leave for 30 minutes to soak, then cut into 4.
